images.title: Pair the primes of 72
images.purpose: Shows the prime tiles of 72 with two 2s and two 3s locked in pairs and one 2 left alone, so multiplying by 2 makes a square.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. The number at the top, one row of prime tiles in the middle, and one short result below.
images.exact_structure: At the top centre: 72 in large dark digits. Below it, one horizontal row of exactly 5 round tiles: two tiles reading 2 joined by a short bar into a pair, then two tiles reading 3 joined by a short bar into a pair, all four filled teal (#0072B2); then, after a gap, one tile reading 2 filled vermilion (#D55E00) with no bar. Below the row, centred: × 2 gives 144. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Multiplying by the unpaired primes gives the smallest perfect square multiple.
images.description: Shows the prime tiles of 72 with two 2s and two 3s locked in pairs and one 2 left alone, so multiplying by 2 makes a square.
images.context: 72 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3; 72 × 2 = 144 = 12². Neutral number, not one of the practice questions.

image_decisions.why: The tool's core move is locking identical primes in pairs and spotting the one left alone.
